nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with a topology, the open profinite completion of $G$ is the limit, in profinite groups, of the diagram of finite quotients $G/H$, where $H$ runs over the open finite-index normal subgroups of $G$ and the transition maps are the projections $G/H \to G/K$ for $H \subseteq K$. Concretely, it is the group of families $(x_H)_H$ with $x_H \in G/H$ that are compatible under these projections, with the…
nodes.title: Open profinite completion of a group

nodes.summary: For every group $G$ with a topology, the image of the canonical map from $G$ to its open profinite completion is dense.
nodes.title: The canonical map has dense image

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with a topology in which multiplication is separately continuous. Then the canonical continuous homomorphism from $G$ to its open profinite completion has dense image.
nodes.title: Density of the canonical homomorphism

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with a topology, this is the functor that sends each open finite-index normal subgroup $H$ of $G$ to the finite quotient group $G/H$ with the discrete topology, regarded as a profinite group, and each inclusion $H \subseteq K$ to the projection $G/H \to G/K$, $gH \mapsto gK$. It is the diagram of finite quotients followed by the inclusion of finite groups into profinite groups.
nodes.title: Diagram of finite quotients as profinite groups

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with a topology. For every $x \in G$ and every open finite-index normal subgroup $H$ of $G$, the $H$-coordinate of the image of $x$ under the canonical map into the open profinite completion of $G$ is the coset $xH \in G/H$.
nodes.title: Coordinates of the canonical map

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with a topology in which multiplication is separately continuous: $x \mapsto ax$ and $x \mapsto xa$ are continuous for every $a \in G$. Then the canonical map from $G$ to its open profinite completion is continuous.
nodes.title: Continuity of the canonical map

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with a topology, this is the map from $G$ to its open profinite completion that sends $x \in G$ to the family of cosets $(xH)_H$, where $H$ runs over the open finite-index normal subgroups of $G$.
nodes.title: Canonical map into the open profinite completion

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group with a topology in which multiplication is separately continuous. This is the canonical map from $G$ to its open profinite completion, $x \mapsto (xH)_H$ with $H$ running over the open finite-index normal subgroups of $G$, regarded as a continuous group homomorphism.
nodes.title: Canonical homomorphism into the open profinite completion

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with a topology, this is the functor from the category of open finite-index normal subgroups of $G$ to finite groups that sends $H$ to the quotient group $G/H$ and sends an inclusion $H \subseteq K$ to the projection $G/H \to G/K$, $gH \mapsto gK$.
nodes.title: Diagram of finite quotients

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ with a topology, this is the set of normal subgroups $H$ of $G$ that have finite index and are open in $G$, ordered by inclusion and viewed as a category: there is a morphism $H \to K$ exactly when $H \subseteq K$.
nodes.title: Open finite-index normal subgroups

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
